races.name: Tramore Directors Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Louiescall
runners_data.note: The confirmed pacesetter, racing from the front under Daniel King for David Harry Kelly who is 0/11 in the last 14 days; has form figures of 2 and 6 over similar Good-ground hurdles in the past and is fresh enough at 18 days, but the trainer's cold run is worth noting against a field of classier-rated rivals.

runners_data.name: Penzance
runners_data.note: Has been placed four times on Good ground at this trip and carries the tongue-strap, making them a consistent type on paper; John Joseph Hanlon's runner is a natural hold-up horse who will genuinely be racing out of their preferred position in a field this congested at the rear, which tempers confidence in a late run materialising cleanly.

runners_data.name: Speed For Fun
runners_data.note: Willie Mullins sends this unexposed five-year-old — only two hurdle runs visible, including a second — with Brian Hayes booked, which is a significant jockey upgrade pointer; acts on Good ground and the form profile suggests there is considerably more to come, making OR 120 potentially lenient.

runners_data.name: Ballybollen
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's prominent-racing five-year-old finished fourth on their only hurdle start on Good ground and Darragh O'Keeffe is an experienced navigator at this track; their natural style of racing close to the pace fits this race shape perfectly and they are one of only two runners whose tactical position maps naturally to the likely race structure.

runners_data.name: Cairo King
runners_data.note: Off the track for 829 days and flagged as a horse that fades in the finish — a massive fitness question hangs over this run and the lengthy absence makes form from three prior hurdle runs almost irrelevant; Josh Younge (7lb claimer) adds uncertainty, though freshness can occasionally flatter on a first-run-back.

runners_data.name: Captain Hanley
runners_data.note: Danny Mullins rides this hold-up type who is actually a natural closer being pushed into a midfield mapping by the field's composition; last run just 8 days ago suggests connections are keeping him fit and busy, but the STYLE_FIT discount and his tendency to fill minor placings rather than win (0 wins from 5 recent hurdle runs) limits confidence.

runners_data.name: Grabat
runners_data.note: Philip Fenton sends a lightly-raced five-year-old with just two hurdle runs, both on Good ground and both finishing in the rear — Niall Moore's 5lb claim is the only positive angle and the form string of 0-6 offers little encouragement in a field where the top weights carry real class.

runners_data.name: Sankofa
runners_data.note: David Harry Kelly's second string alongside Louiescall, flagged as a finisher who fades late — the fade warning combined with a single hurdle run and a form figure of 9 on Good ground suggests this horse is still learning its job; John Shinnick is a relatively low-profile rider and the 13-day turnaround is unlikely to have transformed the picture.

runners_data.name: Bobby Kirova
runners_data.note: A four-year-old with just two hurdle runs, held in by Paddy Cody (7lb claim) for Michael Butler; genuinely wants to race from behind but is being mapped to midfield because the field is overloaded with hold-up types, and with a STYLE_FIT score of 0.91 its natural closing run is unlikely to be executed cleanly from a compressed position.

runners_data.name: Ivatt
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's four-year-old is interesting as one of only two genuine prominent racers in the field, with Danny Gilligan in the saddle — flat form on varied surfaces is the background but the switch to hurdles is unproven, and Elliott's recent form (4/42 in 14 days) gives the yard some live ammunition worth respecting if this runner takes to jumping.

races.paceDynamic: Louiescall is the sole confirmed front-runner and will set a sustainable, uncontested pace from the front, shaping this as a processional gallop rather than a war of attrition. With no rival capable of or likely to pressure them early, Louiescall can dictate fully on their own terms over 2m½f on Good ground at Tramore. The field holds more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear — Bobby Kirova, Penzance, and Captain Hanley are genuine hold-up horses who will be pushed into midfield roles rather than their natural position, meaning the back of the field will be congested and their finishing kicks may be compromised. Ballybollen and Ivatt are the genuine prominent racers who can track the pace organically, and with the tempo likely to be controlled and moderate, horses who sit close to Louiescall in the first half of the race and travel economically will be best placed — this race shape most favours prominent-to-midfield runners who can sustain their effort off a steady gallop rather than true hold-up closers who need a truly run race.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Louiescall Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Louiescall bowls along at a controlled pace and no rival has the speed or intent to press them through the early stages.
scenarios.body: Louiescall sets a comfortable tempo, builds a rhythm over the hurdles, and the race becomes a test of who can sustain their effort in the home straight rather than a true stamina grind; horses close to the pace from early have first run and the lead horse themselves becomes genuinely dangerous. Ballybollen and Ivatt, tracking in the first two, are ideally positioned to pounce in the straight without having been dragged into a battle.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Grind Down Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Ballybollen and Ivatt both press Louiescall from the second hurdle, lifting the tempo and turning it into a more genuine test.
scenarios.body: A stronger gallop develops from an early stage as Ballybollen and Ivatt refuse to concede ground to Louiescall, creating a true pace that stretches the field and tests stamina fully across the 2m½f trip. This plays into the hands of any horse with genuine staying power and class at the top of the weights — Speed For Fun and Ballybollen's De Bromhead-class preparation becomes relevant.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Overrun Field
scenarios.trigger: If the moderate pace implodes in the home straight and the congested midfield-to-rear group swamps a tiring Louiescall.
scenarios.body: With Penzance, Bobby Kirova, and Captain Hanley all crowded into midfield rather than their natural positions, a bunched finish is possible if the pace is truly dawdling and everyone lands in the straight together; however, their redistribution out of true hold-up roles means this scenario is structurally fragile. Penzance, with four placed efforts on Good ground, is best equipped of the hold-up types to deliver late if some daylight opens.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Rank Outsider Springs Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the favourite-market horses fail to stay or jump poorly and a lightly-weighted or unexposed runner capitalises on the chaos.
scenarios.body: A maiden hurdle field at this level always contains unknowns — Grabat, Sankofa, and Cairo King are unproven enough over hurdles that a freak result cannot be entirely dismissed, particularly if jumping errors reshuffle the field at a crucial stage. Cairo King's long absence (829 days) is the biggest wild card and carries the most chaotic potential if freshness translates to speed early.

watchPoints.text: Louiescall's early jumping under Daniel King will define the race tempo — any fumble at the first two hurdles risks disrupting the controlled lead they need to exploit their front-running advantage.

Bobby Kirova, Penzance, and Captain Hanley are all crowded into the same midfield band; watch for traffic problems and interference between them as they compete for the same ground turning into the straight.

Cairo King has not raced in 829 days and is flagged as a finisher who fades — if fitness is short, an early departure or dramatic stopping in the home straight could cause interference for horses directly behind.

Speed For Fun's jumping fluency will be the key to Brian Hayes executing a prominent or handy position — on hurdle debut (or near-debut) any hesitation at the obstacles could drop them out of the race shape where their class is most dangerous.
Trainer David Harry Kelly is 0/11 in the last 14 days — with two runners (Louiescall, Sankofa) in this race, monitor any market move as a signal of which, if either, the yard believes is live.

races.name: Frank Gillane Memorial Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Liberated Light
runners_data.note: Won over this course and distance on Good 9 days ago for the Kiely yard; a hold-up type that will need to find a run late, but recent winning form and Going preference are major pluses — T14 record (0/4) is a concern however.

runners_data.name: Annie's Angel
runners_data.note: Four-year-old lightly weighted at 165lbs, but five runs show no win or place on Good — the sim-going record of 0W0P in 15 comparable runs is a significant flag, and the apprentice claiming 5lbs does not compensate for the form deficit.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Annie's Angel nonetheless catches the eye as our second-ranked runner in a field of fifteen, with experience over today's trip and going and a lively return just 17 days ago; the risk is that her recent finishing positions suggest she needs things to fall right.

runners_data.name: Doctor Confusion
runners_data.note: The one confirmed pace-setter here; De Bromhead runner who has form on this Going (4/5 sim runs) but has yet to win or place on similar ground — a STYLE_FIT note applies as this is a less natural role, though in a field of hold-up types he will lead uncontested and set his own terms.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts, including a pull-up, Doctor Confusion has questions to answer on recent form, though he has run over today's distance and going before and 26 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh; the 165 lb burden is a further ask.

runners_data.name: Ina Mina
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse who won over this exact trip on Good 13 days ago — course form is crucial at Tramore and the sim-going record of 2W4P from 15 runs stands out; John Shinnick in the saddle, and the tongue-tie is retained from the winning run.
runners_data.comment: Ina Mina won last time out and returns on a sharp 13-day turnaround, with experience of both today's trip and going in her favour, but a hefty 165 lb burden and patchy recent form — four starts without a win before that latest success — give reason for pause.

runners_data.name: Pahlavi
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old veteran with 14 sim-going runs suggesting course compatibility, though the recent string of 0s and a pulled-up run raises durability questions over 2m½f today; the OR=95 and apprentice claimer (7lbs) makes the weight manageable but form is unconvincing.
runners_data.comment: Pahlavi has run over today's distance and going, and our rating puts him at the head of this field, but a pulled-up effort last time and a winless recent run of form make confidence hard to fully sustain under a hefty 165 lb.

runners_data.name: Colesberg
runners_data.note: 93-day absence is a concern in a competitive handicap; only one sim-going run on record and the form string of 996-7 offers nothing to recommend — the amateur rider Jordan Canavan (7lbs) keeps weight down but fresh record is unknown.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and ranked 13 of 15 on our figures, Colesberg returns after 93 days off carrying 163 lb, with a string of seventh, sixth, and two ninths making him hard to fancy, though he does have experience on today's going.

runners_data.name: Glendower
runners_data.note: True hold-up type relocated into midfield by the redistribution process — Eoin Doyle runner with solid Good-ground form (3P from 15 sim runs) but the STYLE_FIT discount applies and getting a clear run from a congested midfield will be the challenge.
runners_data.comment: Glendower has run over today's trip and going, and at 95 on our ratings he ranks fourth among 15 rivals, but his recent string of unplaced efforts — including a fifth last time out — makes him winless in his last four starts and that's the primary concern.

runners_data.name: Truckers Cruising
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott runner (T14: 4/42 is solid context) who is a genuine hold-up horse shown in midfield — placed in a deeper field position than natural, meaning the STYLE_FIT caveat bites and its chance depends on a breakaway run that may not materialise in this shape.
runners_data.comment: Truckers Cruising is fit enough on a ten-day turnaround and has experience of today's trip and conditions, while our rating of 103 marks him out as a serious threat in this field; the risk is that recent starts have left him winless and in need of a turnaround in form.

runners_data.name: Lanzhou
runners_data.note: Ran just 3 days ago — extreme freshness concern and the fade-in-finish flag is worrying; a true hold-up type pushed into midfield by redistribution, with a poor sim-going record of 0W0P and a form string that trends backward.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 11th of 15 on our figures, Lanzhou faces a stiff task, though he has run over today's going before and returns just three days after his latest outing carrying 159 lb.

runners_data.name: Owl's Delight
runners_data.note: Prominent-style runner who tends to fade in the finish — five sim-going runs without a win or place and the fade flag is consistent with the evidence; will get a good early position behind Doctor Confusion but may be passed in the straight.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and pulling up two back is a concern, but 24 days gives connections time to have him spot on, and our rating of 92 sits comfortably above his official mark of 84, suggesting there may be more to find.

runners_data.name: Vairue
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old veteran with a 13-day turnaround and a fall on last run — the STYLE_FIT discount applies as this hold-up type is pushed into a midfield slot; notably the only horse with a 15/15 sim-going record, suggesting real course and Going aptitude even if the age is a worry.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and carrying 153 lb, Vairue does have experience over today's distance and going in his favour, though that fall last time out is a concern and his finishing positions make for mixed reading.

runners_data.name: Cinnabar Moth
runners_data.note: Ran only 2 days ago — extremely short turnaround for a five-year-old with no wins from 10 sim-going runs; a true hold-up horse shown in midfield through redistribution, and the tiredness risk from a 48-hour turnaround is real.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and back just two days ago, Cinnabar Moth does have experience of today's trip and going to call on, though a 151 lb burden and a ranking of ninth of fifteen suggest she faces a stiff task finding improvement here.

runners_data.name: Depeche Mo
runners_data.note: 445-day absence is a massive concern — has not raced since a layoff and this prominent-style runner must be heavily discounted on fitness grounds alone, regardless of any form claims.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and returning from a 445-day absence, Depeche Mo faces a stiff ask here, though he has run over today's trip and going before and a third three starts back hints at residual ability; the 144 lb burden hardly helps his cause.

runners_data.name: Surviving Murmansk
runners_data.note: Won over 17f on Good and placed three times from 15 sim-going runs — one of the more solid hold-up types in the field; the redistribution into midfield is the tactical hurdle, but if gaps open from the second-last this horse has the form credentials to capitalise.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 14 of 15 on our figures, Surviving Murmansk looks a tough sell here, though a second two starts back and a run just eight days ago suggests he arrives fit, and he has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Doyen Og
runners_data.note: Fade-in-finish flag plus a 37-day break and a pulled-up run in recent form — the hold-up style forced into midfield by redistribution compounds an already pessimistic profile; Good going is at least compatible but the OR=72 marks the ceiling.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with a pulled up among recent efforts, Doyen Og makes little appeal ranked 12 of 15 on our figures, though she has run over today's trip and going before and returns after a 37-day break carrying 142 lb.

runners_data.name: Maxios Lady
runners_data.note: 324-day absence is disqualifying for serious consideration; the fade-in-finish flag and an OR=72 add further negatives, and the redistribution into midfield from a hold-up role means she faces maximum tactical challenges on return from a near-year off.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and pulled up most recently, Maxios Lady returns after a lengthy 324-day absence carrying 142 lb, leaving plenty of questions to answer; yet to score, she remains unexposed enough to show more than her limited recent form suggests.

races.paceDynamic: Doctor Confusion is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 16-runner field and, crucially, faces no meaningful pressure for the lead — Owl's Delight and Depeche Mo are the only other prominent-style runners, and neither has the profile to seriously contest early supremacy. With Doctor Confusion able to dictate from the front at a controlled, sustainable gallop on Good ground over 2m½f at Tramore, the pace is unlikely to be genuinely searching, which historically compresses the finishing sprint and rewards horses that can track closer to the pace rather than those forced wide or deep off the back. The field holds considerably more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear — Truckers Cruising, Glendower, Lanzhou, Vairue, Cinnabar Moth, Surviving Murmansk, Doyen Og and Maxios Lady are all genuine hold-up horses redistributed into midfield positions they are unlikely to naturally occupy, while Liberated Light, Annie's Angel, Ina Mina and Pahlavi form a genuine hold-up cluster that will need traffic gaps to open late. This race shape — a lone, uncontested leader setting a moderate tempo — strongly favours horses that can sit prominently or in close midfield behind Doctor Confusion and produce a sustained run from the second-last, rather than deep closers who will find the pace insufficient to pull them through a packed field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Doctor Confusion Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Doctor Confusion leads from the front without pressure and the field settles into a moderate, processional tempo that suits prominent trackers.
scenarios.body: Doctor Confusion controls every yard at a gallop that suits his stamina, with Owl's Delight and Depeche Mo unable to challenge, leaving the race to be won by those closest to the leader turning in — prominent-style horses get first run on the hold-up pack.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closers Get Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely steady enough that a trio of well-placed hold-up types find clear ground turning for home and pick off the fading leaders.
scenarios.body: A slow early tempo compacts the field but the final-flight dash becomes a lottery of gaps — horses with recent winning form on Good ground and sharp finishes benefit if daylight appears.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Fresh Legs Win
scenarios.trigger: If Doctor Confusion sets an unsustainable early fraction and stops quickly, gifting the race to a prominent chaser who picks up the pieces.
scenarios.body: A runner tracking Doctor Confusion in second or third absorbs the early pace and surges clear when the leader capitulates — Good ground and the Tramore track's testing final bend punish front-runners who have gone too hard.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — Traffic Blocks Closers
scenarios.trigger: If the congested hold-up group becomes bunched on the approach to the second-last and multiple late challengers are denied a clear run.
scenarios.body: With so many genuine hold-up types forced into midfield positions, interference and checks become likely when gaps close — only the horse that finds daylight earliest benefits, and the winner emerges late from an unlikely position.

watchPoints.text: Doctor Confusion's gallop sets the entire tempo — if Darragh O'Keeffe elects to go overly conservative, the race becomes a sprint from the last and the hold-up pack floods through; watch his position jumping the third-last for early signs of tiring.

Lanzhou (3-day turnaround) and Cinnabar Moth (2-day turnaround) are extreme fitness risks — monitor early market moves and watch for signs of sluggishness in the parade ring, as either could become a hazard in the congested midfield.

With eight or more hold-up types competing for the same late ground, a serious traffic incident is probable in the straight — horses drawn or positioned on the inner turning for home face the greatest risk of being blocked.

Liberated Light won this course and trip 9 days ago and the Kiely T14 record (0/4) is the only negative — watch whether the market shortens it into market-leader territory, as a repeat of that form would be very difficult to beat at this level.

Surviving Murmansk (2nd on going-equivalent form 17d ago) and Ina Mina (winner 13d ago) are the two hold-up types with most recent winning evidence on this Going — if either secures a prominent pitch rather than sitting deep, the race shape upgrades their chance materially.

races.name: Frank King Memorial Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Something Fabulous
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with the best class profile in the field (OR 120, 1W in similar going), John McConnell yard in form at 2/28 over 14 days; 134 days off the track is the one query, but the pace scenario here suits this horse ideally stepping back up in trip.

runners_data.name: Ajp Falco
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who has a documented tendency to fade in the finish; Sean Flanagan takes the ride but the horse's five-run hurdles record shows 0W0P with no better than 6th — its role is likely to serve as a pace-setter rather than a winner.

runners_data.name: Goodmancon
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator with a pair of placed efforts in similar going (0W2P) and a recent 12-day turnaround; Ian Power aboard, and the horse's finishing profile gives it a live chance if the pace gets truly fierce up front.

runners_data.name: L'As de Watt
runners_data.note: Hold-up style with a single placed run (2nd, 2m) in similar going; 5-year-old with a tendency to run mid-division and a claim jockey aboard — the trip (2m5½f) is longer than most of its recent experience suggests suits it.

runners_data.name: Market Ready
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who has placed at 2m in similar conditions with a 7lb claimer up; the step to 2m5½f over hurdles is an open stamina question, but the likely pace suit of traveling just off the leaders could offset that concern.

runners_data.name: South Of Killerig
runners_data.note: Trainer Sheehy sends this genuine hold-up type with a tongue-tie into a race where the held-up ground will be crowded; 84-day break, and the STYLE_FIT flag of 0.90 means its real position in the run is likely to be more forward than suited — discount accordingly.

runners_data.name: Bury Your Past
runners_data.note: Lightly raced 4-year-old for O'Loughlin with an undetermined running style and a fade warning; just the one run at 2m2f hurdles on record and a 7lb claimer up — very hard to assess but the lack of evidence makes this a speculative entry.

runners_data.name: Eyecanboogie
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with one placed run (3rd at 2m) in a similar going; G B Noonan rides and the horse has been lightly raced this season, but a U (unseated) last time is a jumping concern over this longer 2m5½f trip.

runners_data.name: Flowing Fast
runners_data.note: Another lightly raced O'Loughlin runner with a fade warning; the horse pulled up on its only completed hurdle run and has a form string peppered with non-completions — hard to trust even in a chaotic scenario.

runners_data.name: Lady Lena
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner from the Mullins/Hayes powerhouse combination returning after 294 days off; only two hurdle runs to her name (2nd and 3rd), both in decent company — fitness after a long layoff is the single meaningful doubt against an otherwise imposing profile.

runners_data.name: Thelittleredfox
runners_data.note: Denis Ahern-trained 5-year-old with a single run (12th of 17, 2m1f) on record; undetermined style, lightly raced warning, and no evidence of the stamina required for 2m5½f — needs a dramatic leap in form to feature.

races.paceDynamic: Lady Lena (Mullins/Hayes) and Ajp Falco (Kelly/Flanagan) are both confirmed front-runners, meaning the early gallop at Tramore's 2m5½f over hurdles will be genuinely contested rather than dawdling — an honest, pressured tempo is the base expectation from the off. With both leaders committed to setting the pace, the race will be run at a sustained gallop that tests stamina through the final circuit, likely stretching the field and exposing any lack of jumping fluency or finishing reserves. Something Fabulous and Market Ready will push to hold prominent positions just off the pair, adding further pressure to the mid-race fractions and reducing the chance of a false dawdle. This race shape strongly favours horses with proven stamina, reliable jumping, and the ability to travel prominently — hold-up horses will need everything to go right from the back, and the field contains more front-running/prominent types than can all secure their preferred berths, with Lady Lena (class) and Ajp Falco (confirmed pace commitment) best placed to dictate, leaving South Of Killerig — a genuine hold-up type redistributed to midfield — unlikely to get its natural pitch and carrying a meaningful style discount.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Lady Lena and Ajp Falco set a genuine gallop and the race is run at honest fractions throughout, suiting horses who travel prominently into the straight.
scenarios.body: The sustained tempo will expose those who lack stamina or jumping accuracy, and the winner will be one who travels within the first three or four from an early stage and picks up from the second-last.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Gets First Run
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two pace-setters — most likely Lady Lena — asserts from the front and builds an unassailable lead before the final hurdle.
scenarios.body: Ajp Falco's noted tendency to fade late means Lady Lena could capitalise if she leads unchallenged after the last bend, while Ajp Falco drops away; a Mullins/Hayes combination at the head of affairs in a maiden hurdle is not to be dismissed.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Deliver Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace proves truly suicidal — both front-runners burning each other out — and the race collapses in the final quarter-mile.
scenarios.body: Goodmancon and Eyecanboogie have shown ability to finish from off the pace and could pick up the pieces, though this scenario is tempered by South Of Killerig's redistribution out of its natural hold-up role.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaotic/Incident Produces Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves uneven due to jumping errors or fallers among the pace-setters, scrambling the anticipated race shape.
scenarios.body: Lightly-raced unexposed types from the O'Loughlin yard — Bury Your Past or Flowing Fast — could benefit from fortune in a muddled affair, though both carry fade warnings and minimal form evidence.

watchPoints.text: Lady Lena (Mullins/Hayes) returns from 294 days off as the highest-profile runner — watch whether she takes up her natural front-running position cleanly at the start, as any sluggish break could allow Ajp Falco to dictate unchallenged.

Ajp Falco has a clear fade-in-finish flag and is up against a higher-class front-runner in Lady Lena — watch how quickly it capitulates once challenged from the second-last, as it could impede runners coming from behind.

South Of Killerig is a genuine hold-up horse redistributed into midfield due to field congestion at the rear — watch whether Harry Sexton (7lb claimer) can manage the position intelligently, as racing out of role for a 6-year-old with a tongue-tie after 84 days is a compounding risk.

The O'Loughlin pair (Bury Your Past, Flowing Fast) both carry fade warnings and have minimal form — if either shows unexpected early pace or jumping fluency, it could briefly distort the mid-race picture before the stronger stayers assert.

Goodmancon runs for the second time in 12 days, which is worth monitoring in the latter stages — if the quick turnaround has left any residual fatigue, its hold-up finishing run may be blunted over this extended 2m5½f trip.

races.name: Victoria House Tramore Mares Beginners Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Carry On Heidi
runners_data.note: Consistent placed horse for Baragry, runs prominently and handles Good ground well (4/8 on similar), but has not won in a long time and returns after 157 days off; at 2m6f she will need to prove she stays when the pace is genuinely contested.|
runners_data.comment: Consistent without being a winner, Carry On Heidi has finished third in three of her last five starts but remains yet to score, and 157 days off the track is a fitness query; 161 lb is a hefty burden, though she has experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Costanuci
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old who has been placed twice in 15 Good-ground runs without winning; races prominently but trainer Queally sends out a lightly-scored yard (0W/3R in 14 days), and the horse's consistent failure to win despite frequent placed efforts is a concern.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Costanuci nonetheless brings distance and going experience to this assignment, and a second last time out gives her some momentum; the concern is a hefty 161 lb to carry, and she ranks sixth of eight on our ratings.

runners_data.name: Ellens Pride
runners_data.note: Wears a hood and races from the rear; her last seven runs on Good ground have produced no wins and no places, and while she gets a prominent jockey booking with Daniel King, form figures of 04P7 suggest she is out of form and her hold-up style will be squeezed back further given the pace in this race.|
runners_data.comment: Seventh last time and only twice in the first four in her last four starts, Ellens Pride arrives as the bottom-rated runner in this field; she has experience of today's trip and conditions, but it is very hard to make a case for her carrying 161 lb.

runners_data.name: Future Prospect
runners_data.note: Top-rated runner in the race at OR 124, races prominently to lead and has two wins from nine Good-ground starts; Danny Mullins is an elite booking and the Mullins yard is firing at 12/35 in the last 14 days, but La Note Verte from the same yard will fight for the same early position, creating an internal tactical problem.|
runners_data.comment: Consistent and eyecatching, Future Prospect has finished second twice in her last two starts and is drawn from a trainer firing at 34% over the past fortnight; the main risk is that she remains yet to win in her last five starts.

runners_data.name: Kaylasjet
runners_data.note: Five-year-old with jumping issues (tongue-tied) and a string of pulled-up runs; only one Good-ground start on record and that produced no place; the 7lb claimer Ben Kennedy has limited support from the yard (0W/1R in 14 days), and the horse's pattern suggests it will struggle to get competitive.|

runners_data.name: La Note Verte
runners_data.note: Excellent Good-ground record with three wins from eight starts on the surface, and Slevin's booking is strong; will press for the early lead alongside Future Prospect, creating friction that could cost both horses in the finish — but if she gets a clean run to the front and settles, her form figures give her a live each-way chance.|
runners_data.comment: La Note Verte arrives here 25 days fresh, with her trainer firing at 34% in the last fortnight, and consecutive third-place finishes suggest she is knocking on the door; familiar with today's going, she looks well placed to go one better under 161 lb.

runners_data.name: Liss Eile
runners_data.note: Has genuine hold-up tendencies in form but is mapped to midfield here because the field is loaded with horses needing to be towards the rear — her finishing figures (P, 4000) and the fades-in-finish flag suggest even her natural position may not produce a meaningful challenge on these terms; OR 77 is significantly below the main protagonists.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked seventh of eight on our figures, Liss Eile faces a stiff task here; she has run over today's going before and returns after 24 days, but a heavy weight of 161 lb adds further burden to an already unconvincing recent record.

runners_data.name: Miss Fourie
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott runner returning after 323 days off (significant flag) with a placed record on Good ground; races from behind and will need the pace to collapse entirely for her to get involved, which is possible in a contested scenario but not the most likely outcome given her long absence and uninspiring recent form figures.|
runners_data.comment: Miss Fourie has experience of today's going and shapes as a live threat on our rating, but she arrives after a break of 323 days, is yet to win in her last four starts, and that lengthy absence is the key question mark over her chances here.

runners_data.name: Straight Home
runners_data.note: Has three wins from 14 Good-ground starts including over 24f at Gowran and 22f at Fairyhouse, showing genuine stamina; returning after a 426-day absence is the obvious concern, but the Mullins yard's strike rate (12/35 in 14 days) gives confidence this horse is ready, and Brian Hayes is a polished jockey for a patient race-day performance.|
runners_data.comment: Straight Home has won twice in her last four starts, including a victory last time out, and has experience of both today's trip and conditions — backed by a trainer firing at 34% in the last fortnight, she looks a serious threat here, though the 426-day absence is the one obvious question mark.

races.paceDynamic: Future Prospect and La Note Verte are both confirmed front-runners for Willie Mullins, meaning Danny Mullins and J J Slevin will be competing for the early lead from flag-fall, creating a genuinely contested gallop over 2m6f on good ground at Tramore. That rivalry at the head of affairs should produce an honest, unrelenting pace that sustains pressure throughout the final circuit and makes it hard for the lead to be gifted to either horse. Carry On Heidi, Costanuci, and Straight Home will be hunting a prominent position behind the two pace-setters, compressing the midfield and further raising the energy cost for any horse near the front. This race shape — two genuine front-runners pushing each other — classically favours a well-positioned prominent-to-midfield racer who can track just off the friction, absorb the test, and produce a late measured effort rather than a burst; horses with stamina, class, and the ability to cruise into contention without expending energy fighting for position will be best served. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than the map can cleanly accommodate at the head of affairs; Future Prospect and La Note Verte are best-placed to secure their natural lead roles, with Carry On Heidi and Straight Home the most likely to actually hold the prominent slots behind them given experience and trainer firepower.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Stayers Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If Future Prospect and La Note Verte fight for the lead and maintain a strong gallop throughout, draining the field and leaving the race to the most durable stayer.
scenarios.body: The two Mullins lead horses push each other through honest fractions, stretching the field and burning out rivals who try to stay close; the winner emerges from just off the pace in the final half-mile as rivals capitulate. Straight Home and Carry On Heidi, both proven at trips up to 3m on good ground and capable of sitting handy without over-racing, are ideally positioned to benefit from this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Pacer Controls, Kicks Clear
scenarios.trigger: If La Note Verte or Future Prospect establishes an uncontested or lightly-pressed lead and dictates terms throughout.
scenarios.body: One front-runner gets a comfortable rhythm and settles into a controlled gallop, denying rivals the predictable friction that drains the leader; with Danny Mullins or Slevin able to manage their horse's energy, the leader arrives at the last with reserves intact. Future Prospect's course form and Mullins booking give it an edge in this shape, while La Note Verte's strong Good-ground record (3W in 8 runs) makes her equally capable of exploiting a softer pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Emerges Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to completely blow up the front-runners, leaving a gap for a late-running type to come through.
scenarios.body: A fierce battle between Future Prospect and La Note Verte collapses both before the run-in, and a horse who has been held off the pace emerges through the carnage. Miss Fourie has winning form at this class on Good ground and, despite a very long lay-off of 323 days, Elliott's yard has firepower; Ellens Pride could theoretically close from the back, though her recent form is uninspiring.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Attrition Race, Survivors Win
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors, fallers, or a relentlessly high pace causes mass attrition and the race is won by the last standing.
scenarios.body: In a mares' beginners' steeplechase over 2m6f, inexperience over fences can prove decisive at any point in the contest; a chaotic race where multiple runners exit early would open the door for whatever horses are still standing late. Straight Home's proven jumping record and Carry On Heidi's safe jumping style give them the best chance of benefiting from a survival contest.

watchPoints.text: Future Prospect and La Note Verte are both Mullins lead horses — watch for a tactical decision in the paddock or early at the start as to which one is allowed to go forward; if one is deliberately restrained it changes the entire pace dynamic.

Straight Home has not run for 426 days — watch for any signs of rustiness in the preliminaries or early jumping, as a horse this fresh may take time to find a rhythm, but if it travels sweetly it is a serious stayer's chance.

Miss Fourie is 323 days off the track for Gordon Elliott — despite the trainer's firepower, watch her market move carefully; if she drifts in the ring her comeback readiness is genuinely in doubt over 2m6f of jumping.

Ellens Pride wears a hood and has shown a pattern of finishing in the rear half on Good ground — watch whether she is ridden any closer than usual, as any significant change of tactics could indicate a different approach, though her form figures give little cause for optimism.

Liss Eile (OR 77) is considerably below the class of the main pace-setters — watch whether the pace being set by Future Prospect and La Note Verte simply leaves her too far back to matter, confirming the redistribution assessment that she cannot find her natural position in this shape.

races.name: McCarthy's Irish Bar Lexington Handicap Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Intense Approach
runners_data.note: Prominent type with good-ground solid form; McConnell yard in solid recent form (2/28 14-day), ran 8 days ago so fitness is sharp — the U-5-0 recent string is patchy but the 2m6f trip and good turf are ticks, and a handy berth is easily achieved here.
runners_data.comment: Intense Approach carries a hefty 168 lb yet our rating of 129 marks him out as the standout in this field, and he has run over today's trip and going before; the concern is that he remains winless in his last five starts, with a sixth last time out and a fifth earlier his best recent efforts.

runners_data.name: Marv Michael
runners_data.note: The race's sole confirmed front-runner; goes on good turf (14/15 sim-going runs handled it) but has recorded 500-96 in recent form — a 62-day break and a 7lb claimer aboard (Harry Sexton) are factors, and while likely to lead, the STYLE_FIT tag (0.92) reflects that leading a 10-runner handicap chase is genuinely out of his recent operational comfort zone.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and absent for 62 days, Marv Michael nonetheless catches the eye carrying 168 lb with experience of today's trip and conditions, and a rating of 127 suggests he retains untapped potential — though his recent string of unplaced efforts is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Watch The Weather
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse; 10-year-old who handles good turf well (12/15 sim-going) and gets 2m6f on form; the 6-2-0-5-3 recent string shows consistency without dominating, and Paddy Cody (7) is an inexperienced pilot, though R P Cody sends them fit (1/7 14-day) — needs a stronger gallop than this shape guarantees.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out and a second four starts back, Watch The Weather arrives here fit on a 14-day turnaround with experience of today's trip and conditions. Winless in his last five starts, he nonetheless shaped with promise and, carrying 168 lb, our rating of 127 marks him as a lively each-way proposition.

runners_data.name: Nastya
runners_data.note: De Bromhead's mare is a confirmed prominent type with strong good-turf form (3 wins from 5 similar-going starts), won over 24f twice and placed at the same trip — Darragh O'Keeffe is a major booking and she looks the most classically placed of any runner for a race run at this tempo.
runners_data.comment: Nastya has won twice in her last five starts, including a win two starts back, and has experience of today's trip and conditions — she arrives here fit at 25 days' absence and shapes as a genuine threat; the main concern is her pulled-up run last time out.

runners_data.name: Tullyveery Lad
runners_data.note: Only two days since last run is the immediate flag — either a quick turnaround after a minor issue or a yard confident he bounced fine; prominent style suits here and he handles good going (15/15 sim-going runs), but the -502U5 form is modest and a 10-year-old at OR 113 faces younger, higher-rated rivals.
runners_data.comment: Tullyveery Lad has run over today's trip and going, and showed promise with a second three starts back, yet he is winless in recent starts and returns just two days after his last outing, which is a notable concern under a hefty 159 lb.

runners_data.name: Orkneys Jack
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up type with limited good-ground evidence (5/6 sim-going, no wins) — the 5-1-3-5-5 recent run of form shows honest efforts without a win, and at OR 106 with Alan O'Sullivan (5) riding, he needs a thorough pace to deliver and is unlikely to get one today.
runners_data.comment: Landed a win four starts back but has since posted back-to-back fifth-place finishes, and that inconsistency is the concern; he has run over today's going before and 12 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh, though 152 lb is a stern ask.

runners_data.name: General Clermont
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up horse at OR 105 with no wins from 6 similar-going appearances; consistent without threatening and the 6-4-P-9-0 recent form is poor — Sam Ewing takes the ride but there is little in the data to suggest a winning chance in this shape.
runners_data.comment: General Clermont has run over today's trip and going before, though he arrives winless in his last five starts and that pulled-up effort three starts back is a concern; carrying 151 lb tests him further, yet ten days since his last run suggests he is fresh and our rating of 112 offers mild encouragement.

runners_data.name: A Snow White Park
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse in terms of true running style, despite appearing in midfield on the map due to redistribution — Danny Mullins' booking is eye-catching for the Mullins yard (1/4 14-day), and her placings at 20f and 22f on good ground show ability, but the STYLE_FIT tag (0.93) and compressed position are genuine handicaps in a single-paced race.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked ninth of ten on our figures, A Snow White Park is hard to fancy, though consecutive second-place finishes two and three starts back show she can get competitive; the unseating last time is the obvious concern, and 148 lb is no help.

runners_data.name: That's About Right
runners_data.note: A committed hold-up runner by instinct, placed in midfield here only because the map was full of closers — Rothwell has runners (2/33 14-day) and the horse handles good turf (13/15), but the 5-P-0-4-8 recent form includes a pulled-up and a zero, and the STYLE_FIT discount (0.91) reflects how much this race shape works against its preferred pattern.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with a pulled-up effort among them, That's About Right is hard to fancy ranked eighth of ten on our figures, though he has run over today's distance and going before and returns on a quick 19-day turnaround at least fit and familiar with conditions.

runners_data.name: Pourquoi Poi
runners_data.note: Natural prominent-type runner shifted to midfield on the map because the field simply cannot accommodate all its early movers — the 5-year-old has placed at 20f and 25f on good turf for Flynn, but T14 of 0/21 (no winners in 21 runners over 14 days) is a bleak stat, and the STYLE_FIT tag (0.93) signals this race unfolds in a shape that denies its best chance.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked bottom of this field on our figures, Pourquoi Poi faces a stiff task, and a trainer without a winner in 21 recent attempts adds little confidence, though he has distance and going experience to call upon.

races.paceDynamic: Marv Michael is the sole confirmed front-runner and, critically, is the only horse likely to lead without serious competition — with Nastya, Intense Approach, and Tullyveery Lad all prominent types, the early sections will see some positioning battle, but Marv Michael should be allowed to control fractions at a sustainable gallop over 2m6f on good turf at Tramore. That controlled pace benefits horses who can travel efficiently close to the leader rather than those forced to make up ground from deep, placing a premium on prominent-to-midfield runners who stay on rather than those who need a breakneck gallop to generate a winning move. The field holds more hold-up types than can occupy that position, with Pourquoi Poi, A Snow White Park, and That's About Right all genuine closers or prominent horses compressed into midfield, meaning their preferred race shape is unlikely to materialise organically. In a single-paced, well-regulated contest over this stamina-sapping trip, the race shape strongly favours prominent horses with proven good-ground form who can hold a handy berth throughout and grind out a staying effort to the line.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Marv Michael Controls, Stays Win
scenarios.trigger: If Marv Michael dictates an uncontested, honest gallop and the prominent chasers simply cannot lift late.
scenarios.body: Marv Michael sets a controlled pace that suits a thorough stamina test, and the horses tracking in second and third have the clearest passage with the least traffic to navigate; a staying, prominent profile dominates the finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Fight It Out
scenarios.trigger: If Nastya and Intense Approach press Marv Michael into a stronger gallop than ideal, forcing a genuine test of class and stamina.
scenarios.body: Elevated fractions see Marv Michael weakened after the last and the two prominent types who tracked him prove best placed to pounce, with the race resolved between the highest-rated closers from a handy berth.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely strong enough to open the race up for Watch The Weather or Orkneys Jack to deliver from behind.
scenarios.body: A sustained gallop stretches the field and creates a clear run for a hold-up horse with proven good-ground form, though this requires the pace dynamic to be more honest than one sole front-runner typically generates; Watch The Weather's course experience gives it the best late claim.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Market Mover Causes Upset
scenarios.trigger: If a redistributed runner such as A Snow White Park or Pourquoi Poi secures a better pitch than expected and travels supremely to challenge.
scenarios.body: Danny Mullins could manoeuvre A Snow White Park into a more forward position than her usual style dictates, and if the race pans out slowly enough in the early stages she could slot in ahead of the hold-up pack; however, both horses carry STYLE_FIT discounts and the scenario requires multiple things to go right.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Nastya secures a prominent position tracking Marv Michael from the outset — if Darragh O'Keeffe slots her second or third jumping the first, she controls her own destiny in this race shape.
Monitor Tullyveery Lad's fitness signals at the start given only a two-day turnaround since last run; any signs of sluggishness or early reluctance would immediately discount his chance.

Track how aggressively Danny Mullins positions A Snow White Park in the opening half-mile — if Mullins forces her forward from her redistributed midfield slot, she becomes a live factor; if she settles back, the STYLE_FIT discount fully applies.

Marv Michael's jumping should be watched carefully with an inexperienced claimer (Harry Sexton, 7lb) in the saddle on a front-runner over 2m6f — any blunders at pace could unsettle the entire shape and accelerate the race for closers.

General Clermont and That's About Right are both veteran hold-up types who need an honest gallop that this race is unlikely to provide — if they are seen labouring before the third-last, the race is firmly in the hands of the prominent group.

races.name: Heinz Pollmeier Memorial Handicap Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Presenting Lad
runners_data.note: A 10-year-old natural hold-up horse whose best recent effort was a second over 16f on Good; LR 47 days and tongue guard fitted, but trainer McNiff has a cold strike rate and the age profile does not favour catching a well-placed front-runner late.
runners_data.comment: Presenting Lad is our top-rated runner here, and his second three starts back gives him the most meaningful piece of recent form in the field, though he has been winless in his last five starts and returns from a 47-day break carrying a hefty 168 lb.

runners_data.name: Bossing It
runners_data.note: Sean Flanagan takes the ride on this 6-year-old whose second over 17f on Good is the most relevant piece of form in the field; naturally hunts at the rear, so will need the pace to collapse or a perfectly timed run through to hit the frame.
runners_data.comment: Bossing It shaped well when second three starts back and has run over today's trip and going, so the experience angle stacks up; the concern is a tendency to disappoint, and she arrives yet to win in her last five starts.

runners_data.name: Itsalonglongroad
runners_data.note: The lone pace-maker and key race-shaper; 12 years old but has led over this track before, and Good ground is fine for it — the question is whether its stamina holds over 1m7½f when it has raced mainly at shorter in recent starts.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Itsalonglongroad nevertheless holds a rating of 98 here, ranking him second of ten, and he has run over today's trip and going before; the concern is a pulled up finish among recent outings that will need explaining.

runners_data.name: Katherine
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse that has been mapped to midfield only because the field is saturated with rear-division types; its recent form string (774960) is weak, the 13-day turnaround is short, and STYLE_FIT=0.90 reflects that it is unlikely to get its true position here.
runners_data.comment: Carrying 155 lb is the obvious concern, but Katherine's rating of 94 makes her a live threat at the weights, and she returns fit on just 13 days' rest with experience of today's trip and conditions in her favour.

runners_data.name: Kingdom Calling
runners_data.note: Flags a tendency to fade in the finish, which is a significant concern in a race where it will also be racing closer to the pace than it naturally prefers; trainer McCarthy has one winner from nine in the 14-day window but the horse's own form (P0-604) is uninspiring, and the STYLE_FIT discount applies.
runners_data.comment: Kingdom Calling is winless in his last five starts and a pulled-up effort five starts back raises stamina questions, yet he has experience over today's trip and going, returns after a respectable 31-day break, and our rating of 91 suggests he holds more ability than his official mark implies.

runners_data.name: Polly Poppins
runners_data.note: The only confirmed prominent runner apart from the leader, giving it a structurally advantageous position in this race shape; 14 of 15 recent runs on Good ground make the surface a non-issue, though winning form has been absent and it has drifted back in the weights.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Polly Poppins does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and a third four starts back hints at better days; however, a seventh last time out and a burden of 152 lb are clear negatives to weigh against her rating of 87.

runners_data.name: Ray Gun
runners_data.note: A 4-year-old running just two days after its last start, which is a major stamina and freshness concern; hold-up by nature but has never won and has a zero from five TopSpeed record — the 7lb claim from Canavan partially offsets the weight but the profile is raw.
runners_data.comment: Ray Gun has run over today's going before, but two pulled ups and a pair of lowly finishes in recent starts paint a difficult picture, and returning just two days after his last outing asks serious questions of a gelding yet to win in this sequence.

runners_data.name: Nobody
runners_data.note: Prone to fading late and genuinely prefers to race from the back, yet will be squeezed closer to mid-pack than ideal given the volume of hold-up types entered; the STYLE_FIT=0.91 discount and a form line of 5/8/11/16/14 highlight a horse that rarely threatens.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and ranked bottom of this field on our figures, Nobody faces a stiff task here; a 11-point gap to his official rating hints at a horse below his best, though he has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a sharp turnaround of 13 days.

runners_data.name: Ballinaboola Gold
runners_data.note: Bred and raced over much longer trips (20-24f recent history), so stepping back to 1m7½f raises a genuine question about whether the race will suit its grinding, staying style; Danny Mullins is an upgrade in the saddle and Good ground is fine, but the trip shortening is a risk.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with a ninth and seventh among recent efforts, Ballinaboola Gold cuts a frustrating figure, and our rating — ranking her ninth of ten — leaves little encouragement; the plus points are fitness, having run just nine days ago, and going experience.

runners_data.name: Robin Elite
runners_data.note: Three fading finishes flagged, a current OR of 72, and recent races predominantly over 22-24f make this a horse stepping sharply down in trip to a distance that may not allow its stamina to become an asset; mapped closer than ideal to its natural rear position with a STYLE_FIT=0.92 discount in effect.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and including two pulled-up efforts in recent form, Robin Elite is hard to fancy, especially returning just two days after his last outing; the one positive is that he has run over today's trip and going before.

races.paceDynamic: Itsalonglongroad is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 10-runner handicap chase over 1m7½f at Tramore, and with no genuine rival to push it for the early lead, it should be allowed to dictate at a tempo of its own choosing on Good ground. Polly Poppins is the only prominent-style horse mapped behind it, meaning the pace picture is unusually clear for a race of this size. The field is heavily loaded with hold-up types — Katherine, Kingdom Calling, Nobody, Ballinaboola Gold, and Robin Elite are all natural rear-division horses redistributed to the midfield on the map simply because they cannot all occupy their preferred position, and several carry STYLE_FIT discounts as a result. A controlled, sustainable gallop set by Itsalonglongroad with no pressure applied will likely compress the field and create a sprint-finish dynamic that rewards the horse best positioned to attack from prominent or mid-pack early — the race shape most strongly favours front-running or close-tracking profiles given the weight of genuine hold-up types who will likely be further back than ideal.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Itsalonglongroad Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Itsalonglongroad is allowed to bowl along in front uncontested and sets a fair but manageable gallop throughout.
scenarios.body: The 12-year-old has course experience and, facing no pace rival, can conserve energy before kicking clear at the final fence; Good ground suits and its hurdling gate history suggests it handles this track well. Polly Poppins, tracking closely in second, is the likeliest beneficiary if the front-runner ties up, as it has solid Good-ground form at this trip and sits in the ideal position behind a lone leader.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Close Tracker Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Itsalonglongroad sets only a modest gallop and a horse in the chasing pack produces a clean jumping round to reel it in at the last.
scenarios.body: Bossing It or Presenting Lad, both natural hold-up types with decent Good-ground form, could thread through if the pace is slow enough to bring the field together in the straight. Bossing It's second placing over 17f on Good and Presenting Lad's recent placed effort over similar terrain give each a plausible route to the frame in a muddling-pace finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Field Bunches
scenarios.trigger: If Itsalonglongroad is brave early then weakens, causing a concertina effect that brings multiple hold-up horses into contention simultaneously.
scenarios.body: Katherine or Kingdom Calling could pick up the pieces if gaps appear entering the home straight, though both carry STYLE_FIT discounts having been pushed further forward than their natural position warrants. The compressed finish may flatter horses with finishing speed over stamina, but the redistribution discount and their modest recent form limit the upside significantly.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Storms Home Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong enough to string the field out and a lightly-weighted hold-up type produces an error-free round of jumping to close from the back.
scenarios.body: Ray Gun, though returning just two days after a run and with limited turf form, carries a featherweight and a 7lb-claiming jockey; Ballinaboola Gold has better form over longer trips and Good ground, and Danny Mullins gives it professional support. This scenario depends on conditions and mistakes elsewhere that seem unlikely given the race's subdued pace expectation.

watchPoints.text: Itsalonglongroad's jumping accuracy is crucial — if it makes a significant error at any of the early fences it will surrender the race-shaping initiative it depends upon to dictate terms.

Polly Poppins is the horse best placed to capitalise if Itsalonglongroad weakens; watch whether Tiernan Power Roche allows it to track the leader closely or gets pushed back in the early stages by the hold-up cluster.

Ballinaboola Gold's trip shortening from 20-24f to 1m7½f is untested in recent form — if Danny Mullins is seen pulling for position or the horse fails to settle, it is likely running outside its optimal conditions.

Ray Gun running just two days after its last start is the most notable freshness flag in the field — monitor market moves as any late confidence would be significant given the booking of a 7lb claimer.

The redistribution of five hold-up horses into midfield means the early mid-pack could be unusually congested; any scrimmaging or jumping errors in the first half-mile will disproportionately affect Katherine, Kingdom Calling, Nobody, Ballinaboola Gold, and Robin Elite.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Mares Flat Race

runners_data.name: Frau Blucher
runners_data.comment: Unraced and completely unexposed, Frau Blucher makes her debut carrying 165 lb, with everything still to learn but every opportunity to show what she is capable of on this opening appearance.

runners_data.name: Lockeen Rose
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement, Lockeen Rose returns from 239 days off after slipping up on her sole recent start, leaving her form an open book; yet to score, she carries 165 lb and rates as one to watch as she builds experience.

runners_data.name: Moot Hall
runners_data.comment: Moot Hall makes her debut here carrying 165 lb, entirely unexposed and with everything still to prove, but that very inexperience leaves her open to significant improvement as she steps into the unknown.

runners_data.name: Myluckymaker
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement, Myluckymaker showed her best recent form with a second last time out, and returning after 124 days off carrying 165 lb, she remains a mare yet to win but with clear potential to progress.

runners_data.name: Pamelaisbrass
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts, all of which have returned a sixth or worse, Pamelaisbrass makes little appeal at the weights carrying 165 lb, and a speed rating of zero offers nothing to cling to despite her experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Super Freak
runners_data.comment: Super Freak has experience of today's trip and conditions, and her rating of 76 ranks her third among 12 rivals, making her a genuine threat despite a winless run in her last two starts; the main risk is that 165 lb is a hefty burden to overcome.

runners_data.name: Village Dream
runners_data.comment: Village Dream arrives here just 31 days since her last outing, with experience of today's trip and conditions working in her favour, and a trainer firing at 34% over the past fortnight adds strong appeal; though yet to score in recent starts, her top rating of 86 from a 12-runner field marks her as the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Winnie Mcgoogan
runners_data.comment: Unexposed on debut, Winnie Mcgoogan steps into the unknown carrying 165 lb, yet with no form to read against her she remains an open proposition and could be anything.

runners_data.name: A Chairde Go Leir
runners_data.comment: Unraced and wholly unexposed, A Chairde Go Leir steps into the unknown on debut carrying 162 lb, but with no form to weigh up she remains an open proposition with plenty of scope to improve with racing.

runners_data.name: Anna Quaintance
runners_data.comment: Unraced and entirely unexposed, Anna Quaintance steps into the unknown on debut carrying 162 lb, but with no form to weigh up she could be anything and remains one to watch with an open mind.

runners_data.name: Bluebell Breeze
runners_data.comment: Bluebell Breeze has run over today's trip and going, and at 162 lb she faces a stern weight task — though an 82 rating ranking her second of 12 suggests she holds solid claims if that burden doesn't blunt her finishing effort, winless in her last three starts.

runners_data.name: The Two Mary's
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts — a disqualification, a pull-up, and a fall — The Two Mary's brings a troubled recent profile, and with her trainer yet to land one from 24 in the past fortnight, that stable form compounds the concern; the experience over today's trip and going at least gives her fair grounding.
